doc_verification.detail: Reachability: no doc_preflight.json sidecar exists anywhere in the plugin tree; live re-verify performed — the WebFetch tool was domain_blocked for api.qdrant.tech, an alternate web reader retrieved the page successfully (title 'Retrieve cluster details | Qdrant | API Reference'). Version: page carries version selector 'v1.18.x' and the versioned URL v-1-18-x, matching target v1.18.0 (major.minor equal). Content: the page's worked 200 example DOES include all six CollectionClusterInfo fields including "resharding_operations" (array of {direction, shard_id, peer_id, shard_key}) — supporting the flat assertion — BUT the normative schema artifact shipped in-repo for this same version (docs/redoc/v1.18.x/openapi.json:12168-12221, the generator source of this site) lists CollectionClusterInfo.required = [local_shards, peer_id, remote_shards, shard_count, shard_transfers] and declares resharding_operations as "nullable": true and NOT required, so the unconditional containment claim ('response contains ... resharding_operations') is example-derived and overstates the normative required list. Endpoint: the page documents exactly GET /collections/:collection_name/cluster and the runtime path map (scripts/runtime/qdrant.py:44, key collection_cluster) sends the script to that exact path — precise match, no SDK/REST confusion (REST reference page, REST-tested face).

DEFECT: (B) 200 but field types violate the documented shape: ['resharding_operations not list: NoneType'] — Type4_StateLogicViolation (derivative of the same missing key: node.get() on an absent field returns None)

The dispatched state faces (A unknown-name and C post-delete) both returned the documented 404; the DEFECT_FOUND verdict rests solely on the branch-B response-shape check, which the script header explicitly declares in-scope (constraint_ids line 6 includes qdrant_type_cluster_collection_info_001; docstring line 23-25 '+ shape clause of qdrant_type_cluster_collection_info_001 on the positive side')

Multi-script reproduction, same endpoint, same missing-key pattern: output_state_cluster_collection_info_002.log:13 'DEFECT: documented fields missing: [\'resharding_operations\'] — Type4_StateLogicViolation'
output_state_cluster_collection_info_003.log:8 'DEFECT: cluster info 200 after recreate but shape broken: [\'resharding_operations\'] — Type4_StateLogicViolation'

output_state_cluster_collection_info_004.log:7 'DEFECT: 2 x degraded shape on cluster-info 200s during writes — Type4_StateLogicViolation — samples: ["200 missing [\'resharding_operations\']", "200 missing [\'resharding_operations\']"]'

output_semantic_cluster_collection_info_002.log:6 'documented CollectionClusterInfo member \'resharding_operations\' is absent from the 200 payload of an idle (no-resharding-in-flight) collection, while the explicit-tier constraint states the response contains it'

grep across all output_*.log: no response body anywhere contains the key "resharding_operations" — every observed 200 on this endpoint omitted it (deterministic for idle collections), not intermittent

http_semantics.note: The triggering request is a legal GET on an existing collection; no request-side-decidable error (illegal parameter/malformed format/out of range) is involved. The phenomenon is a 200 response omitting a documented optional-marked field — a response-shape question, not an illegal-input-accepted question.

contract_grounding.assertion_text_quoted: response contains peer_id, shard_count (minimum 0), local_shards, remote_shards, shard_transfers, resharding_operations
contract_grounding.note: Dispatch constraint_id was EMPTY in candidates.jsonl (mechanical extraction gap); recovered from the script header (debate_logs/state_cluster_collection_info_001.py line 6 declares both qdrant_behavioral_cluster_collection_info_001 and qdrant_type_cluster_collection_info_001) — the missing-field DEFECT semantics map to the type face, so the type constraint is grounded here. api_violates_assertion=true is literal: the observed 200 body does not contain resharding_operations while the quoted assertion says the response contains it. The behavioral twin ('existing collection: HTTP 200 with cluster info; unknown collection: HTTP 404') was SATISFIED by branches A/B/C of this very log. Material nuance for the auditor: the same version's normative schema artifact (in-repo docs/redoc/v1.18.x/openapi.json:12171-12177,12198) does NOT put resharding_operations in CollectionClusterInfo.required and marks it nullable — the flat contract text is stricter than the normative required list of the documentation it cites.

log: branch B raw 200 body lacks the resharding_operations key; DEFECT lines 8-9 quote the missing field and the derived NoneType type-violation; VERDICT: DEFECT_FOUND is consistent with the raw observation (exit_code 1 per exit convention)

source_grounding.call_chain_traced: REST: src/actix/api/collections_api.rs:198 #[get("/collections/{collection_name}/cluster")] get_cluster_info -> src/common/collections.rs:244 do_get_collection_cluster -> lib/collection/src/collection/collection_ops.rs:460-467 builds CollectionClusterInfo with resharding_operations = shards_holder.get_resharding_operations_info() -> lib/collection/src/shards/shard_holder/mod.rs:534-541 returns None when self.resharding_state is None (idle collection, no resharding in flight) -> types.rs:341 #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] omits the key from the 200 JSON. The observed branch-B body (freshly created idle collection, key absent) is exactly this deterministic path. Face comparison (source-level; live cross-face comparison face_unavailable — sandbox is REST-only): the gRPC face of the same response (lib/api/src/grpc/proto/collections.proto:966 'repeated ReshardingInfo resharding_operations = 6'; conversions.rs:1559-1563 flattens Option via into_iter().flatten()) always materializes the field as an (empty) repeated list, so the omission disposition differs between the rest face (key absent when idle) and the grpc face (empty list when idle).
